changes.headline: Thursday settled at the episode highs and Brent extended overnight; Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters
changes.dek: Thursday settles: Brent Dec26 $113.17 (+$4.35); WTI Dec26 $99.47 (+$2.32). Overnight: Brent $114.47 (+1.2 percent), WTI Dec26 $100.84 (+1.4 percent) at 0639 GMT (Reuters). Dammam toll: 2 killed, 8 injured (updated). Aramco HQ evacuated, no operations disruption reported.. Brent Dec26 settled Thursday at $113.17 (up $4.35, or 4.00 percent), its highest since May 4, and WTI Dec26 at $99.47 (up $2.32), then Brent bid overnight to $114.47 and WTI to $100.84 at 0639 GMT (Reuters). Aramco ordered the evacuation of its Dhahran headquarters on Thursday, staff to work remotely, the first such order since the war began in February; the headquarters houses the operations centre and took extensive fire damage earlier in October, and no disruption to operations was reported. The Dammam airport attack toll was updated to two killed, one an Indian national, making Wednesday's Eastern Province toll four dead with the two Shaybah contractor workers. The US ordered departure was confirmed to cover Saudi Arabia only. The coalition intercepted 11 drones and one ballistic missile on Thursday. The Revolutionary Guards' seven-vessel claim remains unconfirmed on day two, and US Central Command called the mine claims incorrect.
changes.balance_read: The confirmed barrel impact remains zero (Shaybah operations explicitly unaffected, the evacuation a personnel precaution with no operations disruption reported) while the risk impact compounds: an operator evacuating its own headquarters, a record attack tempo, and a premium the deferred curve still refuses to extend beyond the front. The unconfirmed claim's share of the premium shows only in how much refunds if corroboration never comes.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 22 to 23, 2026 (settles; overnight marks; Aramco evacuation, six sources); Saudi GACA with the Indian Embassy in Riyadh, Oct 22; US State Department, Oct 22; US Central Command via Al Jazeera, Oct 22

changes.headline: The waiver's first cargo sailed: 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel loaded at Primorsk for New York
changes.dek: Agioi Fanendes: 40 kt ULSD, Primorsk Oct 22, New York ETA Nov 7. Diesel crack $107.68 on the completed Oct 22 close (3-2-1 $58.52). DOE: up to $150M DPA Title III refinery funding (Oct 22). SPR posted contracts unchanged at 133.56 Mbbl to 13 companies; no award for the Sep 29 round or the Oct 16 re-offer.. A Malta-flagged medium tanker loaded 40,000 tonnes of ultra-low-sulphur diesel at Primorsk on Oct 22 and is heading toward New York, with arrival estimated Nov 7 (Reuters, Oct 23, LSEG shipping data). The sailing matches the date given by Russia's deputy prime minister on Wednesday; the president's alternative timing of two to three days did not govern. No signed supply contracts have been confirmed; the last stated position was that contracts were in the final stage of signing. The announced programme runs 300,000 tonnes immediately, 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes thereafter. The physical constraint is refining capacity: the Ryazan primary unit halted since Oct 15 has no reported restart, and Russia's largest refiner is deliberately stretching repairs from days into months (Bloomberg, Oct 22). The completed Thursday diesel crack closed at $107.68 (3-2-1 $58.52), up from Wednesday's $102.91, and Washington announced up to $150 million in Defense Production Act refinery funding on Thursday.
changes.balance_read: One cargo proves the logistics of the waiver, not its supply: the November tranche is thirteen times this cargo and must come out of a repair queue the operator is deliberately slowing. The US distillate balance now has three federal channels working it in one week (the product reserve exchange, defence-production funding, and the waiver) and the crack still rose after a stock build, which is the market pricing the level of stocks, not the weekly change.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 23, 2026 (LSEG shipping data); Bloomberg, Oct 22, 2026 (refinery repair stretching); DOE press list, energy.gov, Oct 22, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Oct 23, 2026

changes.headline: WCS December tightened on traded volume; the synthetic verdict does not score on zero volume
changes.dek: TMW Dec26 -$27.85 (+$0.50, 515 lots). ARV Dec26 -$19.35 (+$0.40, 1 lot); ARV to TMW December +$8.50. TMS Dec26 +$5.70 (+$0.15, zero lots): verdict does not score, window extends. TMF Dec26 +$5.00 (+$1.00, 150 lots). TMR Dec26 -$1.95 (100 lots).. WCS Dec26 settled at -$27.85 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 22), up $0.50 on 515 lots, the front month's first traded move of the episode after Wednesday's -$28.35 printed on 1 lot. The deferred tenors marked tighter on one-lot and zero-lot volume (Jan27 -$27.00, Feb27 -$25.55, Mar27 -$24.15). WCS Houston Dec26 settled at -$19.35 (ICE ARV settle, Oct 22); the ARV to TMW spread is +$8.50 in December. C5 Dec26 firmed $1.00 to +$5.00 on 150 lots. SYN Dec26 settled at +$5.70 (ICE TMS settle, Oct 22) on zero volume, the third straight zero-volume settle into today's pre-registered verdict date against the +$7.00 and +$6.50 lines; under the volume condition a zero-volume settle does not score, so the verdict window extends to the first settle that actually traded. The last traded SYN settle is Oct 13 at +$4.55 on 40 lots. No public return confirmation for the autumn turnaround windows has been published.
changes.balance_read: The heavies' front month has its first two-sided print of the blowout and it retraced half a dollar, while the synthetic premium the return test grades exists only as an untraded mark below both lines. November's 19 percent light apportionment is the binding near-term fact for the light end; the return question moves to third-quarter volumes on Oct 30 and Nov 3 because the tape is not trading the answer.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD settles, Oct 22, 2026 (TMW, ARV, TMS, TMF, TMR, TMU); Enbridge November apportionment notice, Oct 20, 2026 (standing reference)

flags.title: Hormuz flows above pre-war on exports; attack tempo at a record; seven-vessel claim unconfirmed on day two
flags.detail: Kpler puts Middle East crude exports at 17.3 Mb/d in October, above the 16.9 pre-war average, with Hormuz flows at 11.7 Mb/d, about 82 percent of pre-war and up from 9.75 in September. The maritime security centre counted 12 attacks in and around the Strait last week, a record, and shipping intelligence counts 28 attacks in October. A Kuwaiti products tanker was hit on Wednesday with all crew safe. The Revolutionary Guards' claim of seven vessels hit or mined has no named vessel and no independent corroboration after two days, and US Central Command called the mine claims incorrect. Saudi authorities confirmed Wednesday attacks at Shaybah (operations not affected) and Dammam airport (toll updated to two killed), Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters on Thursday with no operations disruption reported, and the US ordered departure covers Saudi Arabia only. Trade the flow prints and confirmed incidents, not the claims. Trigger: Independent corroboration of any claimed incident, a named vessel, a flow print stepping down, a Saudi statement of facility damage, or an operations impact from the Dhahran evacuation

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: first US cargo sailed on the announced date; contracts unconfirmed; November tranche is the supply test
flags.detail: The first tanker under the waiver loaded 40,000 tonnes of diesel at Primorsk on Oct 22 and is heading for New York, arrival estimated Nov 7 (Reuters, LSEG data). Post-ban loadings to Brazil, Turkey and Morocco were verified earlier in October. No signed supply contracts have been confirmed. The announced programme runs 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes thereafter. The binding constraint is Russian refining capacity: the Ryazan primary unit is halted since Oct 15 with no restart reported, and the largest refiner is stretching repairs from days into months. The import licence runs to Apr 7, 2027 and the waiver has no fixed expiry. Trigger: A first loading for the November tranche, a named US buyer or signed-contract confirmation, a Ryazan restart report, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.title: November apportionment 19 percent lights; December call unregistered; WCS December tightened on volume
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20). WCS Dec26 settled at -$27.85 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 22), up $0.50 on 515 lots, the front month's first traded move of the episode; WCS Houston Dec26 settled at -$19.35 and the December export spread is +$8.50. December's nowcast opens at persistence on November's levels; no December judgment call is registered yet, and December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST. The synthetic return verdict did not score on its Oct 23 date because the December contract settled on zero volume for a third straight day; the window extends to the first traded settle. Trigger: A December judgment call registered, a traded December synthetic settle, or Q3 volumes on Oct 30 that confirm or contradict the turnaround returns

flags.title: Freight correcting from the peaks inside an extreme market; weekly Baltic print lands today
flags.detail: A VLCC on Brazil to China fixed at $48 million on Thursday, correcting the $50 million figure carried Oct 22, and the US Gulf to China VLCC is near $60 million against a $79.6 million record earlier in October, with November Asia-bound US crude orders down about half on the haul cost. Tanker futures rose through March even as spot fell. Gulf to China supertanker freight neared a record $37.37 per barrel this week and war-risk insurance runs to 10 percent of vessel value. The Caribbean to Gulf route remains more than five times a normal market, which keeps competing heavy sellers captive to the Gulf and their length offered at deeper FOB discounts, pressuring WCS Houston pricing; the competing-grade FOB discount gauge has not printed since Sep 22 to 24. Trigger: The Week 43 Baltic weekly reversing the easing, a fresh competing-grade FOB print, or US approval of former shadow-fleet tankers at scale

forward_calendar.what: COT vintage as of Oct 20 and Week 43 Baltic weekly
forward_calendar.detail: Both land Friday afternoon. The positioning vintage is the first that can show whether the escalation buying was short covering or new length, which decides how crowded the premium is. The Baltic weekly extends or reverses the freight correction into a fourth read.

The DNR's formal Notice of Violation of Oct 13 reaches its enforcement conference. Line 5 is operating via its temporary bypass; the conference is a regulatory-track event for the reroute, not a flow event today.

Bids close on the Oct 21 Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels, the first use of the reserve since Hurricane Sandy in 2012), with deliveries to complete by Nov 13. Bid uptake is a dated measure of how tight the Northeast distillate balance remains into winter.

forward_calendar.what: Imperial Oil and Cenovus Q3 results
forward_calendar.detail: The first of the Canadian majors to report the quarter that contains the fall turnaround windows. Upstream volumes are the first public test of whether Syncrude, Horizon and the Suncor plants returned on their guided schedules; no completion notices have been published for any of them. The synthetic return verdict, unscored on zero volume, is carried by these volumes.

The roll of November targets was the consensus at the last meeting, and the standing pause held through October with no delegate news ahead of the meeting. Any change in the production path lands directly on the global balance framing.
Suncor operates Syncrude and the Base Plant and Edmonton refinery windows that ended in mid-October; its Q3 volumes are the closest public read on those returns ahead of September AER data.
Vermilion reports the quarter on Nov 4 (announced Oct 21). A smaller read on the basin than the majors, carried for calendar completeness.
Deliveries under the Oct 21 Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels) are to complete by this date.

December's Mainline nowcast opens at naive persistence on November's print (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert). No December judgment call is registered yet. Nominations close at 0700 MST.
